title: Client-Side
description: Vulnerabilities executed within user browsers, compromising DOM environments, storage, cookies, and cross-origin communications.

attacks.name: Reflected XSS
attacks.desc: Injecting malicious JavaScript via HTTP request parameters that is immediately reflected by the server into the HTML response without adequate encoding or sanitization.
attacks.prevention: Encode untrusted output for its HTML context and keep user data out of script execution sinks.

attacks.name: Stored XSS
attacks.desc: Injecting malicious scripts into persistent data stores (databases, comment sections, profiles) that execute whenever other users view the compromised content.
attacks.prevention: Sanitize any user-authored HTML with a maintained library, then encode it safely when rendered.

attacks.name: DOM-based XSS
attacks.desc: Vulnerabilities where an application's client-side JavaScript reads data from a controllable source (location.search, document.referrer) and writes it to an unsafe sink (innerHTML, eval).
attacks.prevention: Use safe DOM APIs such as textContent and validate URLs before assigning them to browser sinks.

attacks.name: Blind XSS
attacks.desc: Stored XSS payloads that execute in internal administrative or employee dashboards when staff members view user-submitted feedback, tickets, or log viewers.
attacks.prevention: Review delayed rendering paths such as admin dashboards and notification emails; sanitize stored content before display.

attacks.name: Self-XSS
attacks.desc: Tricking a victim into pasting malicious JavaScript code into their browser developer console or into personal account fields only visible to themselves.
attacks.prevention: Do not treat user-pasted scripts as trusted; restrict powerful actions and make the trust boundary clear to users.

attacks.name: mXSS (mutation XSS)
attacks.desc: Exploiting discrepancies between how browser HTML parsers mutate innerHTML and how sanitization libraries inspect markup, resulting in script execution.
attacks.prevention: Use maintained HTML sanitizers that account for browser mutation and test sanitized content in its final DOM context.

attacks.name: XSS via SVG upload
attacks.desc: Uploading SVG image files containing embedded <script> tags that execute script in the victim's browser context when viewed directly.
attacks.prevention: Serve SVG uploads as downloads or sanitize them strictly; prevent active SVG from executing on your origin.

attacks.name: XSS via Markdown
attacks.desc: Crafting malicious Markdown syntax containing raw HTML tags or javascript: URI links that bypass poor Markdown rendering sanitizers.
attacks.prevention: Render Markdown through a maintained parser with HTML disabled or sanitized before insertion.

attacks.name: XSS in PDF generation
attacks.desc: Injecting HTML or JavaScript into server-side headless browsers (wkhtmltopdf, Puppeteer) used for PDF creation, executing code or reading local files via file:// URIs.
attacks.prevention: Treat user-supplied PDF content as untrusted, patch the renderer, and escape text in generated HTML wrappers.

attacks.name: Prototype pollution → XSS
attacks.desc: Chaining client-side JavaScript prototype pollution with existing script gadgets in popular libraries to achieve Cross-Site Scripting execution.
attacks.prevention: Reject dangerous object keys and use safe merge routines before polluted data reaches DOM rendering code.

attacks.name: Client-side template injection
attacks.desc: Injecting template expressions into HTML pages dynamically parsed by front-end frameworks (AngularJS, Vue.js), executing client-side sandbox escapes.

attacks.name: PostMessage misconfiguration
attacks.desc: Listening to window 'message' events without strictly validating event.origin, allowing rogue websites to transmit malicious payloads to cross-window listeners.

attacks.name: DOM clobbering
attacks.desc: Injecting HTML elements with crafted id and name attributes that override global JavaScript variables or properties used in application security checks.

attacks.name: Tabnabbing
attacks.desc: Exploiting links with target='_blank' lacking rel='noopener noreferrer' to allow the destination page to manipulate window.opener.location and redirect the original tab to a phishing site.

attacks.name: CORS-based data theft
attacks.desc: Exploiting overly permissive CORS configurations using malicious JavaScript on a third-party domain to read authenticated responses and sensitive data.

attacks.name: JSONP hijacking
attacks.desc: Exploiting legacy JSONP endpoints that return sensitive data wrapped in client-supplied callback functions, readable cross-origin via dynamic <script> tag inclusion.

attacks.name: CSS injection
attacks.desc: Injecting malicious CSS style rules with attribute selectors and background image URLs to exfiltrate sensitive data (such as CSRF tokens) character-by-character.

attacks.name: Scriptless attacks
attacks.desc: Stealing sensitive page content, form values, and tokens without executing JavaScript by utilizing dangling markup injection, CSS fonts, or standard browser features.

attacks.name: LocalStorage / SessionStorage leak
attacks.desc: Storing sensitive session tokens, JWTs, or encryption keys in browser Web Storage where any client-side XSS vulnerability can trivially read and exfiltrate them.

attacks.name: Service worker hijack
attacks.desc: Registering a malicious Service Worker script that permanently intercepts all client network requests, modifies API traffic, and steals credentials even after leaving the site.

attacks.name: Missing Subresource Integrity
attacks.desc: Loading scripts and stylesheets from third-party CDNs without cryptographic integrity hashes (SRI), allowing compromised CDNs to inject malicious code into the site.

attacks.name: Cross-site script inclusion (XSSI)
attacks.desc: Including sensitive dynamic JavaScript files or JSON arrays from a victim's session across origins using <script> tags to read data via overridden prototype methods.

attacks.name: Autofill data leakage
attacks.desc: Placing hidden form inputs on a page that entice browser password and credit card autofill engines to silently populate sensitive saved user credentials.

attacks.name: Browser cache leakage
attacks.desc: Sensitive authenticated pages cached by the browser bfcache (back-forward cache) accessible to unauthorized subsequent users of a shared workstation.

attacks.name: WebRTC IP leak
attacks.desc: Utilizing WebRTC STUN requests from JavaScript to uncover a client's true local network IP address and real public IP, bypassing proxy and VPN tunnels.

attacks.name: Clipboard hijacking
attacks.desc: Overwriting or reading the user's system clipboard without explicit consent using JavaScript APIs to replace copied cryptocurrency addresses or execute commands.

attacks.name: Third-party script supply chain
attacks.desc: Compromising external marketing, analytics, or customer support scripts loaded by an application to inject credit card skimmers and credential harvesters.
